title: Home Team Science and Technology Agency Bill
what_it_is: Home Team Science and Technology Agency Bill

sections.label: Rising checkpoint traveller volumes
sections.summary: Traveller volumes through checkpoints rose 42% in 10 years, from 149 million in 2008 to 212 million in 2018.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: In the past 10 years, traveller volumes through our checkpoints have risen by 42%, from 149 million people in 2008 to 212 million in 2018.

sections.label: Home Team science technology investment
sections.summary: The Home Team will almost double its science and technology investments from $979 million in FY2019 to $1.9 billion in FY2025.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: I have previously spoken about how greater use of science and technology is key to meeting these challenges.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: That is why the Home Team will almost double its investments in science and technology from $979 million in financial year (FY) 2019 to $1.9 billion in FY2025.

sections.label: HTX building transformative capabilities
sections.summary: HTX will build cutting-edge and transformative capabilities that will augment the Home Team beyond its 27,000 regular and 54,000 National Service and volunteer officers.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: HTX will build cutting-edge and transformative capabilities that will augment the Home Team far beyond our 27,000 regular and 54,000 National Service and volunteer officers.

sections.label: Technology for emergency call processing
sections.summary: With almost 200,000 emergency calls each year, such technology will significantly reduce the time needed to process calls.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: With almost 200,000 emergency calls each year, such technology will significantly reduce the time needed to process calls.

sections.label: Establishing the new agency
sections.summary: The agency will be established by December 2019, and the passage will briefly touch on how and why this is significant.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: I will now briefly touch on how the agency will be established and why this is significant.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: We aim to set up this new agency by December 2019.

sections.label: HTX bringing together officers
sections.summary: As a start, HTX will bring together about 1,300 officers from the Home Team departments.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: As a start, HTX will bring together about 1,300 officers from the Home Team departments.

sections.label: HTX transfer and technology examples
sections.summary: Employees transfer on no worse terms, HTX is an Essential Service under CLTPA, and examples include smart glasses, prison cameras and the IDEAS II System.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Employees will be transferred on terms no worse off than what they enjoyed on the eve of transfer.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: As HTX will support the Home Team’s 24/7 operations, its services will be deemed an Essential Service under CLTPA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Some examples of what have been done or are being worked on include: (a) smart glasses with video feeds and facial recognition technology to assist Police operations; (b) surveillance cameras in prisons that can detect when a person suddenly collapses or when there is a fight so that the surveillance video cameras do not need to be closely monitored round the clock; and (c) the IDEAS II System used by the Central Narcotics Bureau (CNB) which analyses data to establish behavioural patterns and crime hotspots.

sections.label: Contraband cases at checkpoints
sections.summary: Last year contraband cases detected at checkpoints reached the highest annual figure recorded, averaging 300 cases per day.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Last year, the number of contraband cases detected at the checkpoints hit the highest annual figure recorded, averaging 300 cases per day.

sections.label: Computer misuse and e-commerce scams
sections.summary: Computer Misuse Act cases rose 40% from 858 to 1,204, and e-commerce scams rose 11.4% to 2,125 cases with $1.9 million committed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The number of cases under the Computer Misuse Act increased by 40% from 2017 to 2018, from 858 cases to 1,204 cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The number of e-commerce scams also increased by 11.4% from 2017 to 2018, numbering 2,125 cases in 2018, through which $1.9 million had been committed.

sections.label: Bill creates consolidated Statutory Board
sections.summary: The Bill creates a Statutory Board consolidating expertise into one place, instead of individual projects scattered across partners.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Instead of individual projects scattered across different private and Government partners to address different Home Team agency’s needs, this Bill creates a Statutory Board which consolidates this expertise into one place, both in terms of people as well as location, or virtual location.

sections.label: Question on technologists working with officers
sections.summary: A question asks what steps ensure technologists can work closely with ground officers to understand operational needs and requirements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Further, while the concentration, consolidation and collaboration of science and technology teams in the various Home Team agencies bode well for the development of science and technology, I would like to ask the Minister what steps will be taken to ensure that technologists will continue to have the opportunity to work closely with ground officers to understand operational needs and requirements.

sections.label: Questions on agency and partnerships
sections.summary: Questions ask how the new agency works within Singapore's science and technology ecosystem and how it affects or bolsters existing partnerships.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Where there is possibility for utilising technology for other purposes other than Home Team operations, I would like to ask the Minister how will this new agency work within the broader science and technology ecosystem in Singapore to achieve a safe and secure environment for us here in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Because there are current science and technology projects going on among the various Home Team agencies and private and public partnerships, I would like to ask the Minister how this new agency will affect such existing partnerships or even bolster them.

sections.label: Agency plan announcement
sections.summary: The plan to set up the Agency was announced at MHA's COS debate earlier this year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: The plan to set up the Agency was announced at MHA's COS debate earlier this year.

sections.label: Home Team science and technology agency
sections.summary: A dedicated science and technology agency for the Home Team can raise capabilities for the security sector as threats grow complex.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: The range of issues dealt with by the Home Team officers is diverse, and the skillsets of officers must also rise in tandem with the complexity of the threats.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: This is where a dedicated science and technology agency for the Home Team can raise capabilities for the security sector.

sections.label: Data sharing framework question
sections.summary: It asks whether there is also a framework for sharing data and information with other Government agencies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: In addition, is there also a framework for the sharing of data and information with other Government agencies?

sections.label: New agency in ecosystem
sections.summary: It asks how the new agency will work within the broader ecosystem, including with other Government agencies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: How will this new agency work within the broader ecosystem, including with other Government agencies?

sections.label: Malware and data threats
sections.summary: GozNym Malware stole over US$100 million in 2016, and Singapore saw the SingHealth hack and HIV data leak.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For instance, in 2016, GozNym Malware was used to steal over US$100 million from over 41,000 businesses and financial institutions in the US, Canada, Germany and Poland.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In Singapore, the threat is real, as seen in the recent hack on the SingHealth database and the leak of human immunodeficiency virus (HIV)-related data.

sections.label: Crime forecasting pilot project
sections.summary: The VPD ran a six-month pilot of a machine-learned crime forecasting system, and residential break-and-enters dropped substantially.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The VPD undertook a six-month pilot project to evaluate a newly developed machine-learned crime forecasting system that was designed to project predicted crime locations and temporal intervals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The results of the evaluation indicated residential break-and-enters dropped substantially during the pilot study.

sections.label: Predictive policing outputs reviewed daily
sections.summary: The Block Watch Coordinator reviews predictive policing outputs each morning, identifying the top 10% of forecasted locations to mobilise community resources when police are not deployed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In practice, the predictive policing outputs are reviewed by the Block Watch Coordinator every morning, identifying the top 10% of the forecasted locations, with the aim to mobilise community resources for the time period that dedicated police resources are not actively deployed to predicted locations.

sections.label: Pilot study predicted crime locations
sections.summary: The pilot study found that with adequate resources, the top 10% of predicted crime locations could prevent up to 70% of anticipated incidents per two-hour interval.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The pilot study found that when adequately resourced, the top 10% of the predicted crime locations could accurately interdict and prevent up to 70% of the anticipated incidents for each two-hour interval, equal to six to eight locations for every two-hour interval.

sections.label: Lamppost-as-a-Platform and HTX
sections.summary: The Member seeks an update on the Lamppost-as-a-Platform project announced for 2019 pilot rollout and asks whether the Surveillance Programme will fall under the new HTX.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Lastly, before I conclude, I would like to seek an update from the hon Second Minister on the “Lamppost-as-a-Platform” project that was announced last year for pilot rollout in 2019 by GovTech.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Also, with the formation of the new HTX, will such a Surveillance Programme come under the purview of the new agency?

sections.label: New disqualification conditions added
sections.summary: The DSTA Act adds a fourth condition of unpardoned imprisonment of six months, and this Bill adds two new conditions: individuals cannot be a judge or judicial officer, nor disqualified under the Companies Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The DSTA Act adds to that list a fourth condition: unpardoned imprisonment of six months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This Bill we read today adds two new conditions: the individual cannot be a judge or judicial officer.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The individual also cannot be disqualified from serving as a director or manager under the Companies Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: One, why have we added these two new conditions of disqualification?

sections.label: Protocols to safeguard collected data
sections.summary: The Member asks whether the Ministry can share the protocols and structures planned to safeguard data collected, given the potential intrusion on privacy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Given the potential intrusion on privacy that this represents, can the Ministry share the protocols and structures it plans to put in place to safeguard the data it collects?

sections.label: Smart lamp post project
sections.summary: The $7.5 million smart lamp post project awarded to ST Engineering in October last year includes AI-based facial recognition surveillance cameras on 110,000 lamp posts, amongst other smart features.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Let us take the example of the $7.5 million "smart" lamp post project which was awarded to ST Engineering in October last year which includes the installation of AI or AI-based facial recognition surveillance cameras on 110,000 lamp posts around Singapore, amongst other smart features.

sections.label: Oxford study on surveillance
sections.summary: A 2018 Oxford University study found surveillance linked to increased stress, fatigue and anxiety.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A 2018 study by the Digital Ethics Lab of Oxford University found that surveillance has been linked to increased levels of stress, fatigue and anxiety.

sections.label: Surveillance overreach and social compact
sections.summary: The speaker urges the Ministry and new agency to balance street safety with psychological resilience and the social compact.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: What is truly necessary and when does it become a surveillance overreach, especially considering the financial and social costs involved?

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I urge the Ministry and the new agency to be mindful of the delicate balance needed between keeping our streets safe and safeguarding the psychological resilience of our people to maintain a strong social compact.

sections.label: Facial recognition misidentification
sections.summary: Facial recognition systems tend to disproportionately misidentify women and ethnic minorities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Facial recognition systems tend to disproportionately misidentify women and those from ethnic minorities.

sections.label: Facial recognition harms in US and China
sections.summary: Amazon's technology falsely identified 28 members of Congress, and facial recognition targets Muslim Uighurs in China.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: First, last year, Amazon’s face recognition technology falsely identified 28 members of the American Congress as people who had been arrested for crimes, disproportionately misidentifying African-Americans and Latin-Americans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Second, these harmful effects are also already being felt in China, where facial recognition software targets the domestic minority populations, particularly the Muslim Uighur minority in China's "war on terror". "Anomalies" in their behaviour that can trigger suspicion include "dressing in an Islamic fashion and failing to attend nationalistic flag-raising ceremonies".

sections.label: Privacy valued in Singapore
sections.summary: Over 1,600 data protection complaints in 2018 show privacy is valued in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Though there may be a predominant mindset that Singaporeans are not that concerned with privacy, the fact the Personal Data Protection Commission saw over 1,600 complaints on data protection issues in 2018 alone, as mentioned by Minister Iswaran to this House, shows that privacy is valued in Singapore.

sections.label: Data protection and review committee
sections.summary: Given recent data breaches, third-party data protection standards must be ensured, with the review committee reporting by 30 November.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And, given the recent data breaches, we need to ensure high data protection standards by third parties.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I understand that the Public Sector Data Security Review Committee has until 30 November to submit its findings and recommendations to the Prime Minister.

sections.label: Resilient citizenry versus state surveillance
sections.summary: The passage asks whether Singapore wants a resilient, informed citizenry or one that depends entirely on state electronic surveillance and leaves security to the state.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Do we want to build a psychologically resilient and informed citizenry that will also be the ears and eyes for one another in these times of increasing security threats, or a people that depends completely on these ubiquitous electronic eyes on every lamp post and leaving security entirely to the responsibility of the state?

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Do we want to build a culture of respect for privacy, starting with the Government setting an example for transparency and accountability that provides the bedrock of our social compact where there is trust between people and faith in the Government, or a culture of fear and distrust that may impede creativity and innovation?

sections.label: Home Team research staff base
sections.summary: Bringing together over 1,000 research scientists, engineers and technical staff from Home Team departments gives the agency a good base to build on.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The bringing together of more than 1,000 research scientists, engineers and technical staff from the Home Team departments will give the agency a good base to build on.

sections.label: Home Team capability areas outlined
sections.summary: In March this year during the COS debate, Second Minister Josephine Teo shared the need for the Home Team to possess capabilities in biometrics, data analytics and data forensics.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: In March this year, during the COS debate, Second Minister Josephine Teo had shared the need for the Home Team to possess capabilities in the three areas that she had outlined: biometrics, data analytics and data forensics.

sections.label: MHA partnerships and continued collaboration
sections.summary: Second Minister Josephine Teo had shared that MHA has partnered GovTech, DSTA, DSO, ST Engineering and Singtel, and stressed the new agency would continue working across Government and with industry and research institutions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Second Minister Josephine Teo had shared previously that MHA has thus far partnered other Government agencies like GovTech, DSTA and DSO, together with other private sector organisations like ST Engineering and Singtel, to develop these capabilities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: I am glad that in her speech today, the Second Minister stressed that even after the Home Team has established its own Science and Technology Agency, it would continue to work across Government agencies and in collaboration with industry and research institutions.

sections.label: Biometrics benefits and privacy concerns
sections.summary: Biometrics for immigration clearance offers security and productivity gains, but privacy concerns over personal identifiable information mean such technologies must be validated operationally and stakeholder concerns addressed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: For example, as what the Second Minister had shared in the example of the new clearance concept, there are potential security benefits and productivity gains in the development and deployment of biometrics solutions for passenger identity verification for immigration clearance.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: However, as many of the Members have shared in this Chamber today, there will also be concerns around privacy, given the use and collection of personal identifiable information.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Therefore, it is important that such technologies are validated in an operational context for the effective deployment of such solutions and, more importantly, to address stakeholder concerns because, otherwise, we are going to be in a situation where we are concerned about leading-edge, cutting-edge technology, but we are in fear of using it because of the so-called "concerns of the downsides".

sections.label: Balanced approach and three concerns
sections.summary: The speaker urges a balanced approach between concerns and excitement over technology, and raises three concerns about a dedicated Home Team Science and Technology Agency.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: If we do not start, and we do not try and iterate and then learn from it, I think that would be the biggest danger that we will face as a society.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: I do encourage us to take a very balanced approach between the concerns we have as well the excitement around the deployment of technology.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: While I support having a dedicated Science and Technology Agency for the Home Team to augment and maintain our operational edge, I have three concerns which I hope the Second Minister will be able to address and respond to.

sections.label: New Agency Manpower Establishment
sections.summary: The passage asks what the full manpower establishment of the new Agency is.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: What is the full manpower establishment of this new Agency?

sections.label: Employment Conditions Readiness
sections.summary: The passage asks when exact employment conditions will be ready and whether affected staff can decline new terms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: When will the exact conditions of employment be ready so that the affected staff can be apprised of their new terms and conditions and whether they will be given an opportunity not to take up the new terms and stay in their current job roles and schemes of service?

sections.label: HTX Essential Service Classification
sections.summary: The passage raises concern that the Bill amends the CLTPA to classify HTX as an essential service.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Thirdly, classification of HTX as an "Essential Service" and accountability of HTX.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: I am particularly concerned that under this Bill, there will also be a consequent amendment of the CLTPA to classify HTX as an "essential service".

sections.label: HTX Forensic Solutions
sections.summary: The passage states HTX will develop forensic solutions to enhance investigations.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Besides transforming emergency response and enabling new clearance concepts, HTX will also develop forensic solutions to enhance investigations.

sections.label: HTX Essential Service Under CLTPA
sections.summary: The passage states HTX science and technological services are classified as an essential service under CLTPA.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: As the work carried out by HTX officers directly contributes to national safety and security, we have classified the science and technological services provided by HTX as an essential service under CLTPA.

sections.label: HTX Scheme and Transfer Terms
sections.summary: The passage states the new HTX scheme starts December 2019 and transferred officers keep no less favourable terms.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The new HTX scheme of service will be introduced in December 2019, when the agency is set up.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Clause 46 of the Bill ensures that existing officers on the Home Team Specialist Scheme who are transferred to HTX will enjoy terms no less favourable than those enjoyed by the respective individuals on the eve of transfer.

sections.label: HTX funding from MHA budget
sections.summary: HTX funding comes from MHA's block budget, not other R&D funding sources.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The funding for HTX will come from MHA's block budget and not from other R&D funding sources.

sections.label: HTX runs MHA Security Operations Centre
sections.summary: HTX will run the MHA Security Operations Centre to support Home Team operations and protect data.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: To support Home Team operations and ensure that our data is well-protected, HTX will run the MHA Security Operations Centre (M.SOC).

sections.label: Committee deliberating data security measures
sections.summary: The Committee is deliberating measures to improve the Government's data security regime and will report to the Prime Minister by 30 November 2019.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The Committee is currently deliberating on specific measures to improve the data security regime for the Government and will submit a report to the Prime Minister by 30 November 2019.

sections.label: Developing officers and attracting talent
sections.summary: HTX will develop existing officers and attract new talent, starting with about 1,300 officers from Home Team Departments.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: First, developing the existing pool of officers, and second, attracting new talent to join the agency.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: I spoke about how HTX will start off with about 1,300 officers brought together from the different Home Team Departments.

sections.label: HTX recruiting STEM talent
sections.summary: HTX will recruit STEM talent in the next few years, in line with MHA's science and technology investment projected to reach $1.9 billion annually by 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Besides developing existing officers, HTX will also be recruiting STEM talent in the next few years.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: This is in line with MHA's increased investment in science and technology capabilities, which is projected to go up to $1.9 billion annually by 2025.

sections.label: Red Rhino sixth version
sections.summary: SCDF's light fire attack vehicle, known as the Red Rhino, is now in its sixth version.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: SCDF's iconic light fire attack vehicle, popularly known as the Red Rhino, is now in its sixth version.

sections.label: DSTA expertise in C3 marine systems
sections.summary: HTX and Home Team Departments will continue to tap on DSTA in areas where DSTA has deep expertise, such as C3 and marine systems.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: In areas where DSTA has deep expertise and experience, such as Command, Control and Communications (C3) systems and marine systems, HTX and Home Team Departments will continue to tap on DSTA.

sections.label: Forensics and sense-making for agencies
sections.summary: Forensics and sense-making solutions can be used by other agencies with enforcement functions like CPIB and Singapore Customs.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: For example, forensics and sense-making solutions can be used by other agencies with enforcement functions like the Corrupt Practices Investigation Bureau and Singapore Customs.

sections.label: Prudent resource use and MHA location
sections.summary: It also has to do with being prudent in use of resources, and MHA is located in New Phoenix Park.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: It also has to do with how we try to be prudent in our use of resources.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: So, it is in New Phoenix Park where MHA is located.

sections.label: Lamp post sensors trial ongoing
sections.summary: Installation of sensors on lamp posts and backend development is ongoing, with a trial projected to start in the second half of 2019.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: As far as I am aware, the installation of the sensors on the lamp posts and the backend development is currently ongoing.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: I believe that there is a trial that is projected to start in the second half of 2019.

sections.label: Home Team data collection and use
sections.summary: Home Team Departments will continue to collect data on their use, guided by principles of using data securely and responsibly.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: And as I also explained, the Home Team Departments will continue to collect data on their use.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: There are certain instances, for example, viewing of traffic footage that the public has access to.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: But for other kinds of data, we will have to look at them specifically, always guided by the principles of using data securely and responsibly.
